metadata.hardware_observation: EB6 console return reports CE010004/detail00000800: the raw512 CRC predicate alone fails; this audit does not identify who changed the bytes.
metadata.method: Bounded PE/ROM tables and exact PC-relative32-bit load resolution in PROJECTCE .text, plus manual source-window review. PC-relative reference counts are not an exhaustive indirect-call or generated-address proof.

memcpy.destination_findings: Audited fixed destinations include ordinary game user VAs0x000c7af0,0x00830800,0x00821c80..0x00821d80; other inspected destinations derive from stack/caller/object pointers. No inspected call establishes a destination in the raw512 island.

metadata.conclusion: No concrete PROJECTCE or reviewed PLATUTIL writer to0x8100..0x8300 was identified. The raw512 lifetime failure is observed; its modifying instruction remains unknown.

conclusions: The two reviewed WSEGACD memcpy calls read256 bytes from0x8100 into a driver object. They cannot be cited as writers to0x8100.
No concrete writer to0x8100..0x8300 was identified in the reviewed kernel/game paths.
The actual low-memory modification may occur through an unreviewed computed destination or unavailable firmware/middleware body. Its mechanism remains unknown.

A protected authenticated copy preserves the installation-time code identity independently of the mutable execution island. Restoring that exact copy after terminal quiescence can preserve code authentication without accepting changed live bytes. This is a lifecycle correction, not attribution of a writer.
scope_limits: Static source, control and dataflow audit only; no console memory dump, physical watchpoint or full CE/game emulation was available.
Only externally supplied exact source files were parsed. Compressed module sections were not decoded or guessed.
The scalar memcpy call arguments and import ordinal were reviewed; arbitrary caller addresses and BIOS function internals were not executed.
